runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Career form shows two wins at 6f on Good, including a win last time at 6f and a runner-up at the same trip — dropping back to 5f is the only mild query, though has placed here before; Mark Winn takes over for Michael Dods and the T14 rate of 3/30 is modest, but the prominent racing style maps perfectly to this single front-runner scenario.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello partners this Hollinshead three-year-old who has solid 5f Good-ground form (a win, a second, and a third in recent runs), though his true preference is to be produced late from off the pace; in a field stacked with closers, he'll be running closer to the pace than he'd like, which blunts the typical late flourish.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: All five career runs have come on Standard (Tapeta/Fibresand), so today's Good turf is a completely new surface that introduces genuine unknown risk — Connor Beasley's booking is straightforward, but the sim-going score of 1/10 with zero wins or places on turf-equivalent ground is a significant concern; like Dragon Spin, her natural hold-up style is compromised by the compacted field at the rear.

runners_data.name: Ice Cold Alex
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — no analysis applicable.

runners_data.name: U Turn
runners_data.note: 276-day absence is the dominant factor here — Tim Easterby's runner has not raced since a big layoff and David Allan's experience at Thirsk will be crucial in managing a fresh horse; his 5f Good form is actually solid (win and multiple places), and a prominent style suits this race shape well if the fitness holds.

runners_data.name: Riffa Spirit
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie) noted; Zak Wheatley claims 3lb, and the horse's last run — eighth at this trip on Good — is the most recent form pointer; naturally a hold-up horse who wants to come from behind, he finds himself mapped into midfield because the back positions are oversubscribed, which materially reduces the chance of the closing run his style requires.

runners_data.name: Arlo's Girl
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls (5lb claimer) takes the mount for Joseph Parr, whose T14 strike rate is a negligible 0/4; Arlo's Girl has the confirmed front-running role in this race and recent form on Good ground is winless in two tries at 5f, with a sole career victory coming on Standard — the style-fit score of 0.93 reflects she may not be ideally effective even leading, and she is on a career-high OR of 74.

runners_data.name: Bravo Hotel
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this Michael & David Easterby runner returning after a 258-day break — the consistent form figures of 3-3-5-3-3 suggest reliability without a win threat, and the hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuinely testing; Good turf suits (two of her placed runs came on Good), but the long layoff and natural closing style in a race that won't be run flat-out tempers expectations.

races.paceDynamic: Arlo's Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push her from the outside, she is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground at Thirsk's flat five furlongs. U Turn and Simba's Pride will both look to press from a prominent position, meaning there will be a pair of horses tracking Arlo's Girl closely through the early stages, creating a steady but honest tempo rather than a true scorching pace. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Riffa Spirit, Dragon Spin, and Golden Havana are genuine closers by preference but will be shuffled into a midfield slot rather than their natural rear position, reducing their ability to deliver a classic late burst. This race shape — a controlled front-runner setting a fair but uncontested pace — most favours horses who can sit just off the lead in a prominent position and pick off the leader inside the final furlong, making the P-style runners Simba's Pride and U Turn the tactically best-placed horses in this field.

scenarios.body: If Arlo's Girl dictates a fair, uncontested gallop and the race is decided by who tracks her most efficiently.

scenarios.body: If Arlo's Girl goes too fast early and ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for those tracking from midfield.

scenarios.title: Outsider Defies Market

scenarios.body: If tactical chaos — wide draws, crowding through the early stages — scrambles the expected pace hierarchy and an under-the-radar runner exploits the disorder.

watchPoints.text: U Turn has been off for 276 days — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the stalls and the first two furlongs, as a fresh prominent racer can overcook the early pace or miss the break entirely.

Dragon Spin, Riffa Spirit, and Golden Havana are all natural closers compressed into a midfield map position — if they collectively fail to find racing room through the pack at the two-furlong pole, the late headway they need simply won't arrive.

Golden Havana has never run on turf and all her form is on artificial surfaces — any significant deterioration in ground feel or stride pattern in the opening furlong would signal the surface is against her today.

Arlo's Girl's claimer Jack Nicholls (5lb) is a significant booking note — if the front-runner is slightly inconvenienced by an inexperienced stall handler or a slow initial reaction, the uncontested lead scenario that anchors Scenario A unravels immediately.

Thirsk's 5f is genuinely flat and suits a horse who can sustain speed rather than sprint late; monitor how Simba's Pride's jockey Mark Winn positions him in the first furlong — if he drops in behind rather than pressing for the lead, Arlo's Girl gains the easy lead that makes Scenario A most likely.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc

runners_data.name: Vingegaard

races.paceDynamic: Space Bear is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate at a sustainable clip on Good ground over 6f at Thirsk. Frantic and Sugar Baby will press forward into prominent positions behind Space Bear, creating an organised rather than frantic early pace — the tempo is unlikely to be truly fierce, which tends to suit those racing close to the action at this track. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Kings Merchant, Record Day, Harlequin Bay, Taygar and Emperor Caradoc are all natural rear-runners competing for the same small patch of track, meaning several will be forced to race further forward than ideal. This race shape — a single, unchallenged leader setting a controlled pace — heavily favours horses racing prominently in behind, with genuine hold-up horses likely to find the pace insufficient to generate the strong finishing straight they need.

watchPoints.text: Space Bear sets the entire complexion of this race — watch whether Joanna Mason allows a genuine lead or is unexpectedly pressed by Sugar Baby or Frantic in the early stages, as any crowding for the front position transforms the scenario probabilities entirely.

Emperor Caradoc is the most credentialed hold-up horse in the field with a Thirsk 6f Good win on his CV, but he will need a gap to appear in the final furlong — watch whether David Nolan can find daylight given how many rivals are competing for the same late-running lane.

Taygar's Good-ground record (14/15) is extraordinary and seven places in similar conditions demands respect — watch the draw and early positioning, as if Sean Kirrane can find a clear route through, the strike-rate makes this horse dangerous at a price.

Frantic has finished second or third in all four career starts, consistently racing prominently — if George Downing secures a clean position just off Space Bear's heels, that profile of relentless placing form could finally convert on this favourable shape.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Kings Merchant, Record Day, Harlequin Bay, Taygar, Emperor Caradoc) all wanting the same rear positions creates a traffic management risk in the final 2f — any runner with a prominent position and a clear run has a structural advantage regardless of raw ability.

runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a modest recent record, best effort a 3rd on Standard going; David Allan is an experienced handler of this type but the horse's Good-ground figures show zero wins from six attempts, which is a significant caveat.

runners_data.name: Zarvali

runners_data.name: Fuji Mountain

races.paceDynamic: Kosometsuke is the confirmed front-runner here, having won over 7f at Good recently and likely to stride on from the front with Connor Beasley in the saddle — with no other genuine leader to push him, he should control tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop. The prominent brigade of It Just Takes Time, Inside Story, and Zarvali will sit just behind and are well-suited to tracking a steady pace before launching their challenges from the two-furlong pole. This field actually contains more naturally prominent types than can all occupy that position — Woodstock and Gressington have been redistributed on the map because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them all at the front, and Kosometsuke alongside It Just Takes Time, Inside Story, and Zarvali are most likely to actually secure the prominent berths. With one unchallenged pace-setter setting a controlled tempo over 7f on Good ground at Thirsk, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel sweetly into the race and sustain a finishing effort — true hold-up horses relying on a strong gallop to close into are at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Zarvali and Inside Story are both three-year-olds with prominent styles and Good-ground form who could benefit most if Kosometsuke sets a steady, controlled pace — watch whether either gets a clean run from the two-furlong marker.

Woodstock and Gressington are natural forward-going types mapped back on the pace map; if either pushes up aggressively at the start they could disrupt the expected order and compress the lead group earlier than anticipated.

This Farh has won twice in recent form and holds a legitimate chance in a closing scenario, but William Pyle replacing the regular rider is worth monitoring — any positional mistake from the rear on a flat track with no hiding places will be fatal to its chance.

Kosometsuke is the lone confirmed front-runner but carries 144lbs — watch whether Connor Beasley elects to coast at a slow tempo or sets a more genuine gallop, as this single decision shapes which of the four scenarios unfolds.
Mr King is flagged for fading in the finish and has been running over 8-10f — the 7f trip here may be too sharp for him to be competitive in the closing stages regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony

runners_data.name: King's Crown

races.paceDynamic: Spendmore Lane is the confirmed lone front-runner here, carrying early-speed headgear and a clear profile to bowl straight to the lead unchallenged from the gates over this flat Thirsk 5f. With only one genuine pace-setter, this race will likely be run at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front, with Spendmore Lane dictating from flag to furlong-pole without ever being seriously pressured into going too hard. Beaumadier, Military Girl, and King's Crown will push into prominent positions behind, while the hold-up contingent — Marajito, Le Beau Garcon, and Emerald Harmony — will be forced to settle and come from off the pace in the final two furlongs. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate: Khabib, Pal Joey, and Hover On The Wind are all redistributed from their natural positions, meaning the midfield will be more congested than the pace map implies, and Spendmore Lane and Military Girl are most likely to actually secure their forward positions. A controlled gallop on good ground at Thirsk favours horses that can race prominently and sustain their effort — front-to-middle profile types who get a clean passage are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Military Girl has won her last two on good ground over 5f and gets Connor Beasley — if she tracks Spendmore Lane cleanly, she is the most dangerous challenger to the leader entering the final furlong.

Congestion in midfield is a real risk: Khabib, Pal Joey, and Hover On The Wind are all genuine hold-up or prominent types pushed into the same space, creating the potential for interference or traffic issues in the straight — watch for bumping or checked runs around the two-furlong pole.

Spendmore Lane's good-going record is sparse (2 runs, 0 wins, 1 place) — if the ground is quicker than he handles, his ability to sustain the lead to the line is uncertain despite his front-running profile.

Beaumadier returns after 84 days off and has not raced on good ground in his last five starts (all standard); watch to see whether he handles the quicker surface before assessing his chance in running.
Le Beau Garcon ran just five days ago — monitor for any signs of tiredness in the closing stages as he attempts to produce his hold-up finish having had very little recovery time between runs.

runners_data.note: Roy Bowring's 4yo has placed twice on Good ground over 5f and carries 134lbs, but a 26-day absence and an OR of 63 suggest the handicapper has this about right; hold-up style means it needs something to go wrong up front.

races.paceDynamic: Crocus Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f handicap and, with no genuine rival to push them off the front, Jack Nicholls should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates — three wins from five career starts show this horse knows how to lead and see it out. The danger is that Knicks, Midnight Lir, Blue Lakota, Albegone and others are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed in the pace map because the field contains far more want-to-sit types than it can accommodate at the rear; in practice several of them will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would choose, adding a degree of pressure to Crocus Time that the raw map does not fully capture. Irish Dancer and Startling are the most likely horses to actually secure prominent positions alongside or just behind the leader, with Startling's yard in strong form (T14: 3/7) and Irish Dancer's course-and-distance win this season making both credible pace-pressers. On Good ground at Thirsk over 5f, a controlled tempo set by a single front-runner with prominent-racing types tracking closely is the dominant shape, and the tactical profile that benefits most is the horse who sits second or third, travels smoothly, and has the finishing speed to collar the leader in the final furlong — making front-to-prominent runners the primary target profile.

watchPoints.text: Crocus Time's early sections are key — watch whether Jack Nicholls is allowed a solo lead or whether Irish Dancer and Startling crowd the pace immediately, as any meaningful pressure on the front-runner transforms the race shape entirely.

Startling is a NON-RUNNER flag — confirm raceday market activity and field confirmation, as the jockey entry shows NON-RUNNER(5) which may affect pace mapping and compress the prominent berths further.

With five horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types, watch the draw and early movements; if several rush forward to avoid being buried, the opening furlong could be considerably faster than Crocus Time's connections anticipate.

Dandy Dinmont recorded a 5f Good-ground win here recently — if Nigel Tinkler has timed the return well and Jary gets a clean passage, the horse is capable of outrunning its odds in a pace scenario that collapses late.

Irish Dancer's tongue tie is retained and the 3lb claim from Wheatley is meaningful at this level; watch the market for any sign of stable confidence, as the horse's prominent style is the best fit for the pace shape this race is likely to produce.
